anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1.

## Common preamble (all variants)

1. In the session cwd, run `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, which returns `/work/widget/.git`. So **ROOT=/work/widget**.
2. Run `git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree`. It returns empty, so this is not a submodule.
3. Read the overrides file. It contains only a test runner, with no `home:`, `create:` or `destroy:` keys and no wrapper.
   - Home resolves to `$ROOT/.worktrees/<name>`.
   - `<name>` is `fix/retry` with `/` replaced by `-`, giving `fix-retry`.
   - **Home=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry**.
4. In cwd `/work/widget`, run `git -C /work/widget fetch origin`. It succeeds.
5. Check the ordered stops for every admitted PR (#12, #13, #14):
   - **Fork check:** `isCrossRepository` is false for all three.
   - **Head objects:** `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q <head>^{commit}` succeeds for aaaa…, bbbb… and cccc….
   - **Remote branches match heads:**
     - `origin/fix/retry` = aaaa…
     - `origin/fix/cap` = bbbb…
     - `origin/fix/retry-docs` = cccc…
   - **Worktree list:** I ran `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain`. Variant results are below.

The single-PR ancestry stop asks whether the local branch is an ancestor of `origin/fix/retry`. It would refuse *any* combined home tip, so it does not fit here. For an admitted array, I evaluate local `fix/retry` as a recovery candidate instead. It is accepted only if all of these hold:

- The original home head is an ancestor of the local tip.
- Every first-parent commit after that head is a two-parent merge of an admitted head.
- Each such merge carries provenance.

Nothing gets reset or rebased.

## Variant A: selected home exists, clean, on fix/retry @ eeeeeee

**Worktree list.** It shows `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on `refs/heads/fix/retry`. That is the selected home, so the "checked out elsewhere" stop does not fire.

**Recovery proof (cwd /work/widget):**
- `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa fix/retry` exits 0. The original home head is preserved.
- `git -C /work/widget rev-list --first-parent aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..fix/retry` returns only `eeeeeee…`.
- `git -C /work/widget rev-list --parents -n 1 eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee` shows exactly two parents, aaaa… and bbbb…. Both are admitted heads.
- `git -C /work/widget log -1 --format=%s eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee` returns "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12". Provenance holds.
- `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb fix/retry` exits 0. #13 is already merged, so I create no new commit for it.
- `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc fix/retry` exits 1. #14 is still pending.

The recovery candidate is accepted.

**Selected-home row:**
- **Dirty-tree ask:** `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain` returns empty and exits 0. The tree is clean, so no ask is needed.
- **Fast-forward:** `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --ff-only origin/fix/retry` reports already up to date, since origin is an ancestor.
- **HEAD check:** HEAD is `eeeeeee`. It descends from `headRefOid` aaaa… through admitted merges only, so it is accepted as the recovered head.

**Captured values:**
- PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (the original head is retained). WAVE_BASE_SHA must later descend from it.
- `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main` gives BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd.

**Remaining admitted head (cwd /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry):**
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` merges cleanly as **fffffff**.

**Base merge:**
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` merges cleanly as **1111111**. Record: `merge: 1111111`. No conflicts occurred, so no helper was dispatched and no scoped tests were run.
- The unresolved-thread query from the reference ran for #12 with no threads returned. Record: `Threads: none`.

**Step 4 report:**
```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ eeeeeee
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
Base SHA: ddddddd
Recovered: eeeeeee = merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12 (already ancestor, no new commit)
Merged: PR #14 head ccccccc -> fffffff
merge: 1111111
Threads: none
Ready to implement retry-cap rework (#12 with #13, #14)
```

## Variant A-no-worktree: local fix/retry @ eeeeeee, no worktree anywhere

**Worktree list.** `fix/retry` is not checked out anywhere, so that stop does not fire.

**Local-branch inspection.** I ran the same five commands as in Variant A:
- The is-ancestor check of aaaa… against `fix/retry` exits 0.
- The first-parent walk returns only `eeeeeee`, which has two parents, aaaa… and bbbb….
- The subject is "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12".
- bbbb… is an ancestor. cccc… is not.

The recovery candidate is accepted.

**Fresh-creation checks:**
- `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain` returns empty and exits 0, so the source is clean.
- The home is the default `.worktrees/` path, so I ran `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees`. It succeeds, so nothing needs to be appended to `.gitignore`.
- The current branch equals the default branch `main`, so there is no provenance note.

**Provisioning.** I deliberately skip `update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry origin/fix/retry`. It would move the branch back to aaaa… and discard the recovered merge, which amounts to a reset. Instead, I check out the existing branch:
- `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry` succeeds.
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns eeee…, which equals the local tip. It is accepted as the recovered head.

**Captured values.** PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaa… (full) and BASE_SHA=dddd… (full).

**Merges (cwd /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry):**
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` gives **fffffff**.
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` gives **1111111**.
- No PR #13 merge is re-created. Threads: none.

**Step 4 report:**
```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ eeeeeee
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
Base SHA: ddddddd
Recovered: eeeeeee = merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12 (already ancestor, no new commit)
Merged: PR #14 head ccccccc -> fffffff
merge: 1111111
Threads: none
Ready to implement retry-cap rework (#12 with #13, #14)
```

## Variant B: local fix/retry tip 2222222 after eeeeeee; session in linked worktree "other"

**Session worktree.** The session's `other` worktree, at caller HEAD 9999999, is not the selected home on `fix/retry`. It is never adopted. ROOT still resolves to /work/widget through the common dir.

**Stops.** The fetch, fork, object and remote checks pass as described in the preamble. The worktree list shows no checkout of `fix/retry`.

**Local-branch inspection (cwd /work/widget):**
- `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa fix/retry` exits 0.
- `git -C /work/widget rev-list --first-parent aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..fix/retry` returns `2222222`, then `eeeeeee`.
- `git -C /work/widget rev-list --parents -n 1 2222222` shows a single parent, `eeeeeee`.
- `git -C /work/widget log -1 --format=%s 2222222` returns "unrelated cleanup".

That commit is not a merge of an admitted head, so the recovery proof fails. The local branch is not the PR head and not an admitted combination of PR heads.

**Stop.** This happens before any write, any `worktree add`, any `update-ref`, and any merge:

> `local branch fix/retry is at 2222222, not an ancestor of origin/fix/retry (aaaaaaa); rework needs the PR head.`

Nothing is reset, rebased or deleted. Deciding what to do with `2222222` (move it to its own branch, or drop it) is left to the user, after which the run can be retried.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

**The supplied PR-head procedure does not support the requested recovery of a local merge stack.** It requires the selected checkout’s HEAD to equal PR #12’s original head, `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`. I therefore cannot report successful recovery in A or A-no-worktree. The narration below follows that procedure, including the case’s synthetic command outcomes.

All commands below have this unchanged process cwd:

```text
<scratch>
```

Every repository operation explicitly selects `/work/widget` or the selected home.

## Common resolution and commands

The PR-head reference replaces generic linked-worktree reuse. Thus B’s unrelated linked worktree is not adopted.

Resolved values:

```text
ROOT=/work/widget
PR=acme/widget#12
headRefName=fix/retry
headRefOid=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
baseRefName=main
NAME=fix-retry
HOME=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
```

The admitted companion heads remain:

```text
acme/widget#13: fix/cap        bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
acme/widget#14: fix/retry-docs cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

There is no configured multi-PR recovery exception in the supplied skill. Neither those heads nor the titles change its exact-head requirement.

For each independent variant, I run these commands, in order:

```bash
git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse fix/retry
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor fix/retry origin/fix/retry
```

The common directory resolves to `/work/widget/.git`; the submodule guard is empty. Fetch succeeds, the original head exists, and `origin/fix/retry` resolves to the supplied `aaaaaaaa…` head. The local branch exists. I take the ancestry command’s success as stipulated by the case.

## A — selected home already exists

The worktree listing identifies the selected home on `fix/retry`, so there is no competing-path stop. The local branch resolves to:

```text
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
```

Commands continue:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --ff-only origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

Status succeeds with empty output. Merging the already-contained original head creates no commit. HEAD remains:

```text
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
```

**Stop:**

```text
Selected home /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry has HEAD
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee,
but PR #12 requires
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.
```

The approved-looking merge subject and parent list do not waive the procedure’s equality check. I do not merge #14 or `origin/main`, fetch review threads, or issue a Step 4 readiness report.

## A-no-worktree — local branch exists, selected home does not

The listing contains no checkout of `fix/retry`. Local inspection above resolves its tip to:

```text
eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
```

After the stipulated successful ancestry check, the prescribed existing-local-branch provisioning commands are:

```bash
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
git -C /work/widget update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

Status is clean. The ignore check succeeds, so no ignore-file write is needed. Provisioning succeeds and the selected home is listed.

The case expressly stipulates that post-create HEAD is nevertheless the original local tip, `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`. I use that synthetic observation rather than substitute an expected Git outcome.

**Stop:**

```text
Post-create head mismatch at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry:
expected aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa;
observed eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee.
```

I leave the tree intact. There is no Step 4 readiness report and no subsequent merge.

Notably, this prescribed `update-ref` path does **not** implement provenance-preserving recovery of the local merge stack. That requested recovery would require a different procedure.

## B — pre-write refusal

The local branch inspection resolves its tip to `2222222` as supplied. Before provisioning or merging, I inspect the proposed retained history:

```bash
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..fix/retry
```

The observation contains the ordinary single-parent `2222222` commit, subject `unrelated cleanup`, followed by the described merge commit `eeeeeee`.

**Pre-write refusal:**

```text
Refusing recovery of fix/retry: its retained first-parent history includes
ordinary commit 2222222 (“unrelated cleanup”), not just the supplied PR-head
merge provenance. The prescribed PR-head procedure supplies no exception
for accepting that history instead of original head aaaaaaa.
```

I do not adopt the unrelated `other` worktree, update refs, provision a checkout, merge, reset, rebase, delete anything, or invent a replacement commit. No Step 4 report is emitted.
